rationale: Evidence: iteration 3 (683.18, best so far) finished the oval 20/20 (mean 1.79 s) and the s-bend 20/20 (mean 2.21 s), but the slalom still failed 0/20. Its progress rose from 0.28 to 0.36, yet max_error was 0.0646 (above the 0.06 m limit) and line_loss_events rose from 1.0 to 1.45, so the robot still leaves the line on the sharp slalom alternations. Lowering speed and raising kd did not clear the slalom limit on their own. The Evaluator's rule for this case (slalom progress rising, still off track with max_error above 0.06) is to lower kp and speed together: kp 3.0 to 2.6 reduces corner gain and overshoot, and base_speed 1.3 to 1.2 reduces the drift through sharp direction changes. Changes: kp 3.0 to 2.6 and base_speed 1.3 to 1.2. Geometry, ki 0.05, kd 0.8, sensor_weights and line_loss are unchanged from iteration 3, so the race isolates the corner-gain and speed change. Expected result: slalom max_error below 0.06 with some slalom finishes, slalom line_loss_events at or below about 1.0, oval still finishing (about 1.9 to 2.0 s, well under 3 s), and s-bend finishing at or above 0.9. Risks: the lower kp may slow the oval and s-bend response, and the 1.2 speed lengthens the finish time. If the oval finish rate falls below 1.0, return base_speed to 1.3 and keep kp 2.6. If the slalom still ends off track with max_error above 0.06 while line losses stay high, the next test is kd 0.9 at base_speed 1.2. Measurements requested: full set, so the per-track max_error, line_loss_events and completion_time can show whether the slalom limit is being met.
